relevance_note: Case report of a child with a TNFAIP3 variant ('Whole exome sequencing revealed a heterozygous mutation in the affected TNFAIP3 gene'), plus a literature table of 15 paediatric HA20 patients with individual-level data.
method_note: Read the whole paper by hand; a Python script in my scratch directory assembled the rows and copied Table 3 row segments (label through cell) by slicing the Markdown lines; I checked its output against Table 3 and every span is verified verbatim by script. Index child labelled 'patient' (rule 5; the Figure 1 legend calls him 'the first witness', which reads as a role, not a label); his father (carrier) and mother (sequenced in Figure 1) are 'father of patient' and 'mother of patient'. Table 3 literature patients are labelled by the number in its 'Patients' column (e.g. '1 (2)' -> '1'); the number in brackets is the reference, recorded in source_reference_in_review. Table 3 legend defines 'Y, yes; N, no' and 'age, age at diagnosis', so N cells are excluded (legend quoted as second span) and Age (y) is age at diagnosis; '—'/'−' cells in Others/Treatment and 'Without elaborating' are not reported. Narrow-vs-broad rule applied strictly: N for 'Recurrent oral ulcers', 'Recurrent genital ulcers', 'Rash', 'Arthritis' and 'GI ulcers' gives excluded phenotypic rows but leaves the broader checklist items not reported; only 'Recurrent fever' N excludes the checklist item. Checklist mappings I judged: 'Pericardial effusion' -> pericarditis or other serositis; 'Insulin-dependent diabetes' -> type 1 diabetes; 'Autoimmune thyroid disorder' -> autoimmune thyroiditis; 'small vessel CNS vasculitis' -> CNS involvement and vasculitis; 'cytopenias', 'hepatitis' and 'Hypothyroidism' are not stated as autoimmune, so those checklist items stay not reported. 'Pharyngalgia lymphadenopathy' (no comma) split into two features. Ages 5.1 and 4.6 recorded as P5.1Y and P4.6Y (decimal years, not converted). Index child: the only age given is at admission ('3 years and 6 months old'), about 10 days after fever began; recorded as age at onset; no age at diagnosis or last evaluation is stated. Lab abnormalities are recorded against the printed reference ranges in Table 1 and the authors' text. Grandparents: 'This child's grandparents tested negative for the gene' - number and side of family not stated, so no rows were created (this would otherwise be in scope); it is quoted in the child's parental_testing_statement. The father's zygosity and the father's own inheritance are not stated (left not reported); the mother's TNFAIP3 result is shown only in Figure 1 and not stated in text, so she has no variant row. Other-gene variant: Table 2 'Alpha thalassemia gene SEA deletion (Southeast Asian type)' is attributed to the child; no gene symbol is printed. Contradictions/discrepancies: (1) text says 'high IgE and IgA on admission' but Table 1 IgA is 1.47 g/L within the 1.45–3.45 reference; recorded as observed per the text, with the table value as detail. (2) Text says 'IL-6, IL-4, and IL-10 all showed elevations' but Table 1 has no IL-10 entry. (3) Discussion says 'no special abnormalities in rheumatologic immune indicators', while the authors also state abnormal ANA, ANCA and thyroid antibodies (Table 1 ANA 33.3, P-ANCA weakly positive); both rows are emitted; I read 'no special' as 'nothing specific' and kept autoantibodies observed in the checklist. (4) 'This child's grandparents tested negative ... suggesting that the mutation came from the father' does not follow if they are the paternal grandparents; recorded verbatim, no de novo call for the father. (5) 'oral and pendulous ulcers': 'pendulous' site unclear; not mapped to genital ulcers. (6) The review says adult-onset patients were excluded, but its reference [4.] is titled 'A case of adult-onset still's disease ...' while Table 3 lists patient 4 at age 4; recorded as printed. n_patients_reported left null: the authors state one new case and '15 pediatric cases' from the literature but give no total for the document.
